hook: Drop a WhatsApp chat export, see who owes you what — one HTML file, nothing uploaded.
Paste plain text, get a printable Easy Read page: one idea per block, big type, a picture slot each.
Paste a WhatsApp order chat, get a clean order sheet, a baking/pick list and print-ready invoices — offline, one HTML file, nothing uploaded.
Drop a sliced .3mf/.gcode and get a print receipt: time, grams of filament, and cost, entirely offline.
Collapse a million log lines into a dozen templates — and diff a good run against a bad one. Offline, zero dependencies.
Full-screen signs, scoreboards, queue numbers, countdowns and timers where the URL is the app — send the link, send the sign.
Drop a .gguf; learn if it fits your GPU, at what context, and whether its chat template is broken.
Chrome is dropping XSLT — turn your styled RSS, Atom and sitemap XML into a static, JavaScript-free page browsers can still show.
Paste a letter, see exactly what makes it hard to read, and fix it — EN/ES/DE, offline, no AI.
Search any binary file by value — int/float ranges and timestamps in any encoding — not just exact bytes.
Drop in a Claude Code session log and see the exact turn where your prompt cache broke, what changed, and what it cost.
See your stacked-PR branch chain, spot drift, get the rebase commands — zero deps, read-only.
Turn a WhatsApp order chat into an order sheet, pick list and CSV — one HTML file, offline, no API.
Type a cron schedule and a time zone — see what it actually fires, including the runs DST silently skips or doubles.
Subtitles drift or jump? Pin two cues to where they belong and re-time the whole file — offline, one HTML file.
Open a HAR file privately: waterfall, filter, copy-as-curl, strip the secrets, and diff two captures — one HTML file, nothing uploaded.
Paste an nginx config, get a Caddyfile — plus an honest list of what couldn't be translated and why. One HTML file, nothing uploaded.
Drop a CSV, see exactly what Excel would silently destroy (leading zeros, long IDs, SEPT1 -> 1-Sep), and get a copy it can't ruin. One HTML file, nothing uploaded.
Drop a Toggl, Clockify or Harvest export and see the hours you worked but never billed — plus the invoice note to send. One HTML file, nothing uploaded.
See where your repo's churn, ownership and risk live — one git log, one self-contained HTML treemap.
Drop your old and new site URLs, get a reviewed redirect map plus Netlify, Vercel, Apache, nginx and Cloudflare rules — chains and loops caught, nothing uploaded.
A deliberately vulnerable toy MCP-style tool server to break and fix: path traversal, command injection, tool rug-pulls and localhost Origin bugs, with hints and tested solutions. Local only.
Audit GitHub Actions workflows for pwn requests, script injection and unpinned actions — one dependency-free file, SARIF output, nothing leaves your machine.
Gatehouse 1.1: now also catches cache poisoning, artifact poisoning and secrets/inputs expanded into scripts — still one dependency-free file.
Audit your package-lock.json for supply-chain red flags and review lockfile diffs in PRs — one offline, dependency-free file.
Check your repos for the Next.js image-optimizer RCE that npm audit may not tell you about — offline, zero dependencies.
A 200-line vulnerable API lab for JWT alg:none, BOLA, SSRF and mass assignment — with switchable fixes and tests. Zero dependencies.
Audit npm and Yarn lockfiles for supply-chain red flags and review lockfile PR diffs — offline, zero dependencies.
Audit the MCP, Claude Code and rules-file config in your repo for hidden Unicode, inline secrets and risky permissions — offline, zero dependencies.
Leashcheck 1.1: paste your AI-agent config (MCP, Claude Code, rules files) in the browser and see risky settings. Nothing is uploaded.
Gatehouse 1.2: paste a GitHub Actions workflow in your browser and see risky patterns (pwn requests, script injection, unpinned actions). Nothing is uploaded.
Paste your site's response headers, get a grade and copy-paste fixes for nginx, Apache, Netlify and Cloudflare — offline, in English or Spanish.

Paste what an MCP server tells your AI and see hidden instructions, invisible text and data-leak tricks; save a fingerprint so you notice when a tool changes after you approved it. Offline, English or Spanish.
The yfinance docs told you to download a file that no longer exists and left your install broken. A two-line fix, tested in a clean environment and sent upstream.

Your security headers may be there and still not work: browsers use only the first HSTS, enforce every CSP copy, and silently drop a __Host- cookie with a Domain. Headerfix 1.1 tells you which, and gives the fix for your server.

Since May 2026 DMARC has a new standard (RFC 9989) and pct= no longer exists. Type your domain: Remitente counts your real SPF lookups, checks DMARC, DKIM and MTA-STS the way Gmail and Outlook do, and gives you the exact line to fix. In your browser, no account.

wordpress.org closes plugins for security issues and WordPress never tells you. Paste your Site Health info: Vigía shows which plugins are vulnerable, actively exploited (CISA KEV), closed or abandoned, and what to do. In your browser, no account, your versions never leave your computer.

Let's Encrypt no longer emails you before your certificate expires, and certificates will last 47 days by 2029. Type your domain: Candado shows when your padlock expires, whether renewal is stuck, and whether your CAA or DNSSEC will make the next renewal fail. In your browser, no account.

AI assistants that summarize your email or browse for you read all the text, including what is hidden with font size 0 or white on white. Paste a page or an email into Trasluz and see what only the AI reads, and the orders hidden in it. In your browser, nothing uploaded.

You pushed a .env by mistake or got the "we found your key exposed" email. Paste the file into Derrame: it tells you which keys are in it, which are dangerous and which are public by design, and the order to rotate them with each provider's official link. In your browser, nothing uploaded.

Saturday open-source contribution: a one-line fix for a dead link in the better-sqlite3 docs, plus the lesson from a link that looked dead and was not (always confirm a 404 with a browser user agent).

Do you own domains that never send email (the .com next to your .cl, an old brand)? "v=spf1 -all" alone does not stop someone from forging them. Remitente 1.1 checks the three records that do, shows which DMARC policy your subdomains really get under RFC 9989, and explains records broken by copy and paste. In your browser, no account.

Do you get a daily email from Google or Microsoft titled "Report domain" with a .zip nobody opens? It is not a scam: it is the DMARC report of your domain. Recuento reads a whole month of them in your browser and tells you who is sending as you, which service to fix, and whether you can move to quarantine or reject. No account, nothing uploaded.
Paste the page source of your Shopify store and see who can run code in it: apps, old script tags that stop on 1 March 2027, hand-pasted scripts and imitation addresses. Nothing is uploaded.

Paste the page source of your website: see every outside script, mixed content and the http:// links Chrome now stops at, and get a report-only Content Security Policy that will not break Google Tag Manager, Analytics or Stripe. Nothing is uploaded.

Before you click "Allow" on an AI assistant or automation, paste the permissions it asks for on Google or Microsoft 365: see what it could do with your email, files and calendar in plain words, the narrower permission to ask for, and how to take the access back. Nothing is uploaded.

Before you push, publish or deploy, paste the list of files that are leaving: see which ones usually hold passwords and keys (.env, SSH keys, Firebase service accounts, FTP settings, backups) and whether they end up in Git, your npm package, your Docker image or your public website, with the exact line that stops each one. Nothing is uploaded.
